OMX_PARAM_CONTRACT_UNITS.doc: The units of org.openmixer.param-contract/1, the code its get() reports for a parameter's plain value, by token: the LV2 unit a face writes for a descriptor unit (units:db is db), 0..24 the LV2 units one to one, 0x100 and up the vendor block of units LV2 has none for, append-only. A token is served when it has a code here; none is 0.

docs.none: no unit: a plain number, a switch, an index
docs.frame: audio frames (samples) at the running rate
docs.db: decibels, a relative level or a gain
docs.coef: a coefficient, a plain multiplier (1 is unity)
docs.degree: degrees of arc or of phase
docs.dbfs: decibels relative to full scale, 0 the largest sample, a level (vendor block)
docs.dbu: decibels relative to 0.775 V RMS, an analogue level (vendor block)
docs.ratio: a ratio, n to 1, as a compressor states it (vendor block)
docs.lufs: loudness units relative to full scale, ITU-R BS.1770 (vendor block)
docs.dbPerOct: decibels per octave, a filter slope (vendor block)
docs.dbPerS: decibels per second, a rate of level change (vendor block)
docs.dbtp: decibels relative to full scale, true peak, ITU-R BS.1770 (vendor block)
docs.lu: loudness units, a loudness difference, ITU-R BS.1770 (vendor block)

STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES.doc: The standard sample rates (Hz) the desk recognises, the pro-audio superset. One source of truth for the clock controller's `clock.allowed-rates` seed, the force row's validation ceiling and the device-rate probe fallback. What the operator is OFFERED is always the DEVICE's own `supportedRates`; this is the ceiling a write is refused by, never a menu.

STANDARD_QUANTA.doc: The quanta (buffer sizes, in frames, a count with no unit of its own) the console offers: the set a measurement grid or a probe takes its quanta from, beside the rates STANDARD_SAMPLE_RATES lists. A consumer that measures at fewer quanta takes a subset of this list and states it; it never keeps a list of its own. What the operator is OFFERED is still the engine's own choice, this is the ceiling a request is refused by.

VERB_HOSTS.doc: The hosts a verb's implementedBy names (docs/contract-dir.md): the programs a controller sends mod-host's protocol to. A verb states what each one owes it; a host the verb leaves out owes it nothing.
VERB_HOSTS.why: A host's verbs were typed twice, in plugin-hostd's protocol.h and in omx-clap-core's command table; a verbs item declares them once, and the hosts it names are a closed list, so a misspelt host is refused rather than read as a host that owes nothing.

PARAM_SCALES.doc: How a host draws a parameter: linear, logarithmic (a frequency, a time) or in discrete steps. The words omx-plugins' declarations and plugin-hostd's protocol use; a travel names its own with `scale`.

PARAM_UNITS.doc: The one list of standard units (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-20, standard vocabulary in one place; docs/units.md): each word's `x-symbol` is its symbol as written (`%`, `""`, `dB/oct`), the word a name the wire can carry, its `x-dimension` what it measures (a word of PARAM_UNIT_DIMENSIONS) and its group its scope (a word of PARAM_UNIT_SCOPES). The schema's $defs.unit enum is the symbols of the `param` units and $defs.descriptorUnit those of the `descriptor` units and `unknown`, in this order (tools/unit-enum.mjs). The list only grows: a unit is appended, never moved or removed. A level's own spellings (an LV2 unit, a CLAP unit code) map onto these ids at that level.
PARAM_UNITS.why: The unit list is declared once (omx-panel docs/behaviour-core.md, decision 3): the panel core and descriptor validation read one list.
